text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock gained modestly today, continuing a strong recovery from last week's dip. The broader refining sector has benefited from tight diesel and heating oil inventories—diesel storage sits at just 103 million barrels as heating oil demand spikes 59% above last winter—creating better margins for refiners who turn crude into these products. Refineries are running at 95.2% capacity, leaving little spare production to meet this demand surge.

However, headwinds are building. Russian crude production has rebounded sharply to 8.73 million barrels per day, pushing global oil markets back into surplus according to recent reporting, which typically pressures refiner margins over time. With oil inventories already elevated at nearly 694 million barrels and crude prices moderating to $89.62 a barrel, the tight supply conditions that have buoyed refiners lately may not last.
